Kotor 2. Playing that game is like reading a piece of classic literature. At first you like depth and slow pacing and you pat yourself on the back for enjoying a classic. But halfway through it starts getting dry and you start to understand why modern lit/games are they way they are.

Being older I can understand the dialogue more and actually know what's happening this time instead of just flying around talking to jedi who for some reason wont tell you what happened. The MMO Starwars. Being an ex WoW player, I had high hopes for a Star Wars version, but it just never lived up. I went in knowing it wasn't going to be a polished, but without the player base and the teamwork from the well established guild system that WoW has, it just couldn't do it for me.
It's the opposite for me. That game was a little frustrating at launch, but now it's pretty stable and solid IMO.
Assassin's Creed. I played the first game, enjoyed it. Played the second game, loved it. Played brotherhood, got bored. Saw the annual releases, gave up completely.
Metro 2033. I read the book first and was looking forward to a video game adaptation. I did not enjoy the video game adaptation.
Darksiders 2. It started off alright "I am DEATH", then moved to "Why is death so whiny?", and about the third area "Wheee...fetch ANOTHER three random ass items to unlock the boss..."
For some reason I enjoyed darksiders2 it felt like I was playing god of war.

Homefront. The graphics were decent, the story starts out interesting, but then it just goes off the rails.

At the very start, you're immediately thrust into this really grisly world where people are being rounded up and killed in the streets. Fast forward a bit, and you encounter absolutely gigantic, mass graves. Finally, you're supposed to be all sad when someone in your "group" dies, but at that point, you're already numb. You already saw people getting executed in the street and dumping grounds for their bodies. All of that's in addition to the fact that the game is ridiculously short. I don't even think it took me 10 hours to get through. You don't even have time to reach a point where you care about anyone in your "group" because you've probably only spent a minute or two of actual play time even interacting with them. The whole game ended up being disappointing.

Honestly that's what most of the main fps game campaigns feel like. The only interesting thing about them is usually the variety of different maps. Other than that they are mostly just a linear, quick, fun shooting gallery with a story that serves little more than a justification for all the action (I loved JC2 for at least being self-aware about that). Anyone expecting something greater from an fps game will often find themselves disappointed.

There have been a lot of great FPSs with much longer, better stories. The Half Life series (obviously), Bioshock, Borderlands, etc. Even Wolfenstein New Order's story was great, although a little short. The Last of Us (3rd person but basically an FPS) was absolutely incredible. Exceptional story telling and the game was beautiful and fun to play. Good games are out there, but too many people are just accepting completely garbage stories like they make up for the okay game play.

I don't know if I outright hated it but I lost a lot of interest in Bioshock as I was playing it. I bought it after playing the demo and loving it. By the time the game was done I found myself thinking "Well thank fuck that's over."
Ni No Kuni: Wrath of The White Witch. Really enjoyed the story, direction, art style and gameplay until the introduction of capturing the Pokémon like creatures. Completely killed it for me.
Final Fantasy series. Some where between 9 and 10 I realized I just didn't like these games anymore. I tried 12 I think but still, meh I just have no desire to play these.

Minecraft. At first I thought there were lot of potential for growing in depth and complexity (I started in beta) but it never really happened; what I find particularly irritating is the lack of competence by the developers, not only technically (the game is still riddled with huge bugs after years from release) but also regarding gameplay basics, not to mention the fact they completely lack a direction and are hostages of their own users. To put it simple: a huge game with no designer; it bothers me a lot.

I really hate that Minecraft never really implemented the cohesive feeling of progression that say, Terraria has. I know they really tried to give it an 'ending' a while back, but the impression of your character gradually getting stronger and facing increasingly difficult enemies just never really panned out. Once you've got a base set up, there's little impetus to leave it.

Exactly. It's like they're trying to shoehorn an adventure/survival game in what is essentially a Lego without Lego parts, without even having the slightest idea how to accomplish the result.

I could write a book about it. For example, 3 tool tiers out of 5 that get useless a few minutes after starting the game, with the 2° best tier available since the beginning and the best one in a matter of hours; after that, all the advancement you can aspire to is available by grinding, while exploring and fighting is much less desirable; once you obtained enough OP gear, you can travel to the final boss and kill it quite easily (it doesn't seem 1.9 will change that too much). Everything you do in the meanwhile is either completely optional (who needs a beacon, really) or a trivial chore (eating). What is it, 20 hours of staying inside your base and the immediate surroundings before game over?

The non-creative part of this "game" (it's more like a toy IMO) is saved by the immense customizability allowed by 3D party developers that first created servers than created APIs to support modding and then created an incredible amount of mods, no matter if Mojang supported almost none of the above and kept changing the code base every few months. These people are the only reason why I keep playing this thing once in a while, but it's so hard to hack a good game out of this mess.

I have reasons to think no one in the Minecraft team knows the basics of Game Theory; they're just modders and coders, after all, not artists or designers.

Yesterday I was randomly browsing Don't Starve wiki and it was refreshing to see how someone still cares about properly designing games instead of loose frameworks where people can frolic aimlessly. It's not a sin but not my cup of tea either, too bad I believed Notch when he said he wanted a 3D Dwarf Fortress meets Dungeon Keeper...

Wildstar it had a skill based combat system that could have been used to make a dynamic mmo with amazing player versus player. What we got was a spammy rpg where aiming didn't really matter, the difficulty was all over the place, the storyline was terrible, I would rather resub to wow than ever play that game again and I already made a vow to never play wow again(going on 4years).

I've got clause in my vow that says if they remove Pandarens and daily quests, I'll come back.

So yeah, 'never' for me, too.

Thirty hours after giving up and accepting it was a never ending grind fest I finished it.

At least the last boss and the ending were pretty cool.

Terraria. Weirdest thing, I used to really enjoy it, then an update changed how the rocket boots worked and I didn't enjoy it anymore.
